name: sqlite-catalog-contracts-history-review
goal: SQLite catalog units declare accurate readable contracts, and history-index source changes retain committed relocation review evidence.

evidence: The feature commit adds six derived SQLite/catalog function manifests and changes two previously moved history implementations. Expected behavior is declared, readable unit contracts and committed review entries tied to each changed definition while original move hashes remain intact.

The generic contract test reports missing descriptions but does not pin the six new catalog units as a group; the existing service index test detects stale definitions but the review ledger guard does not require a review when one is absent. Added focused metadata and review-ledger assertions while keeping shared test support unchanged.

Committed red checkpoint 96cdc762b: the unchanged unit-index guard reports two moved-source definition gaps, the new review test reports the missing buildHistory review, and the SQLite contract checks report 32 metadata gaps. The isolated Vitest command installs dependencies from the committed lockfile first.

The six SQLite/catalog manifests now carry declared responsibilities and field descriptions. Both changed history implementations are linked to full source commit hashes, with current definitions recorded and original move proofs preserved.

The unchanged portable manifest and review-ledger regressions passed at fix commit 288d69edb in the same isolated runtime fingerprint as red 96cdc762b. The broader unit-index ownership test passed separately in the repository worktree; an earlier snapshot attempt could not run it because exported snapshots have no .git directory.
